title: 10 Principles of Rapid Skill Acquisition
coreMove: Turn a competence target into a low-friction practice loop that produces corrected reps quickly.
sourcePressure: The source lists the rapid acquisition operating system: lovable project, one skill at a time, target performance level, deconstruction, critical tools, removed barriers, made time, fast feedback loops, short bursts, quantity, and speed.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating the principles as a checklist for feeling prepared rather than a loop that increases useful contact with the skill.

sourceAnchors.name: 10 principles of rapid skill acquisition
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen support lists the chapter principles from project choice through deconstruction, friction removal, feedback, short bursts, and quantity-speed practice
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The ten principles are less like advice on a poster and more like a bench setup: target, tools, clear space, feedback, reps.

sourceAnchors.name: target performance level
sourceAnchors.detail: the source names a target performance level as one of the core rapid acquisition principles
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A target performance level tells the practice session what finished enough will look like before enthusiasm starts wandering.

tryThisNow: pick a goal and practice now
remove distractions with no named barrier

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: paramedic trainee practicing radio handoff clarity
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner who needs a narrow professional subskill under time pressure
exampleSpecs.stakes: unclear handoffs waste seconds when a patient is transferred
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Emily strips the skill to a thirty-second SBAR radio handoff, records five attempts, and uses the instructor stopwatch and playback as fast feedback
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a scuffed radio clipped beside a laminated SBAR card

exampleSpecs.domain: craft brewery quality tech learning yeast-cell counting
exampleSpecs.audience: a technical learner whose project needs the right tool before reps can count
exampleSpecs.stakes: a batch decision depends on whether the count is trustworthy by Friday
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Mikkel borrows the hemocytometer first, clears one bench, and repeats only the counting grid until his supervisor can compare results
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a glass counting chamber drying beside a labeled yeast sample

exampleSpecs.domain: legal clinic volunteer learning intake triage questions
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader who needs one usable service skill instead of whole-field knowledge
exampleSpecs.stakes: walk-in clients are being booked with the wrong attorney slots
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Grace asks a supervising attorney to mark the three triage questions that sort urgent eviction from general advice, then practices only those calls in short bursts
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a pink hearing notice sliding under a scratched intake window

exampleSpecs.audience: a hands-on learner who keeps expanding into the whole bicycle
exampleSpecs.stakes: a charity repair day needs ten safe commuter bikes by Saturday
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Hugo predicts watching repair videos will help more, then improves when he isolates one barrel-adjuster loop and gets immediate chain-noise feedback
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a rear wheel ticking against a bent repair stand tray

exampleSpecs.domain: wedding officiant learning one bilingual ceremony segment
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader whose lovable project gives practice emotional pull
exampleSpecs.stakes: the couple wants the ring exchange understood by both families in two weeks
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Rachel limits the target to the ring exchange, removes unused readings from the folder, and rehearses ten short takes with feedback from the groom's aunt
exampleSpecs.firstImage: thin gold rings resting on a printed bilingual vow page

exampleSpecs.domain: library staff member learning 3D printer first-layer setup
exampleSpecs.audience: a public-service learner who needs repeatable tool competence
exampleSpecs.stakes: patrons keep losing reservations when prints fail in the first ten minutes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lin traces three failed prints to bed leveling, tapes the setup card to the machine, and does six first-layer checks instead of browsing model catalogs
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a curled strip of blue filament lifted from a glass print bed
